all.title: chrome.json chrome.list_sound_but_not: the example is mathematically false
all.detail: The string says «ln после exp даёт z». That is ln(e^z), and it is not z on the natural domain: ln(e^z) = z − 2πik in each strip (2k−1)π < Im z < (2k+1)π. So the composite is not rational, and the lamp is right to stay off. The example therefore shows nothing about incompleteness. The English has the same error («exp followed by log»). The correct example is the other order. exp(ln z) = z on D = ℂ minus the cut, so it agrees with the rational function z, yet neither step is rational (Шабат: exp(Ln z) = z for every branch).
all.fix: Например, exp после ln даёт z, но ни один из этих шагов не рационален, поэтому «рациональная функция» не указана. Also tell the owner that the English needs the same fix: «log followed by exp returns z».

all.title: guide-tour.json tour.phase_style_cauchy_plots: the zeros are on γ, not inside
all.detail: The tour scene 'roots' (work/xt/src/tour.js line 36) uses the unit circle and F = z³ − 1. The three zeros are the cube roots of unity, so |ζ| = 1: they lie on γ itself, not inside it. «(видны три нуля)» is false, and so is the English «inside, with its three zeros».
all.fix: Стиль «Интеграл Коши» строит фазовый портрет интеграла $\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_\gamma\frac{F(\zeta)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta$ по замкнутой кривой $\gamma$ — здесь это единичная окружность. Внутри он равен $F(z)=z^3-1$, снаружи — $0$; три нуля функции $F$ лежат на самой окружности $\gamma$. Чтобы взять другую замкнутую кривую, выделите её. (Alternatively, change the scene to r = 1.2 and keep «видны три нуля».)

all.title: Notation: I18N.notation() turns \log_2 into \ln_2 (export.drawn_as_level_sets)
all.detail: I ran proto/i18n.js. notation('\lfloor\log_2|f|\rfloor','ru') returns '\lfloor\ln_2|f|\rfloor'. «ln₂» is meaningless. The note on export.drawn_as_level_sets and GLOSSARY 2.2 both say «\log_2 stays». The regex \\log(?![A-Za-z]) also matches before «_».
all.fix: In RU_TEX, use the pattern `\\log(?![A-Za-z_])` (or skip when the next character is `_`). Expected output: `\lfloor\log_2|{f}|\rfloor`. Add the test eq(I18N.notation('\log_2|F|'), '\log_2|F|').

all.title: math.json: «сравнение» means a congruence in Russian mathematics (7 ids)
all.detail: In Russian, «сравнение» is a congruence a ≡ b (mod m) (Виноградов, «Основы теории чисел»). An error such as «Функция не может содержать сравнений» reads oddly to a mathematician. The same file already says «Нужно неравенство для области» (math.region_needs_comparison_e_2), so the wording is not even consistent. The usual term is «неравенство», or «знак сравнения» for the symbol. Also add «сравнение» to GLOSSARY 1.15.
all.fix: math.function_cannot_contain_comparisons: «Функция не может содержать знаков <, >, =». math.combine_comparisons_with_or, _2, _3: «Соединяйте неравенства словами and / or / not». math.comparisons_are_only_allowed: «Неравенства и уравнения допустимы только в формулах областей». math.region_needs_comparison_e: «Область задаётся неравенством, например |z| < 1». math.comparison_has_no_derivative: «У неравенства нет производной». math.comparison_has_no_inverse: «У неравенства нет обратного».

all.title: math.json export.solid_paths_t_h: «пунктирные» does not mean dotted for Russian readers
all.detail: The caption tells dotted lines from dashed ones. In common Russian usage «пунктир» is the dashed line, so «пунктирные» and «штриховая» look like the same kind of line. ГОСТ 2.303 names the dashed line «штриховая». The unambiguous word for dotted is «точечная». As it stands, the caption describes the figure wrongly.
all.fix: Сплошные линии — пути $t\mapsto H_t(z)$ отмеченных точек до значения $t$ в кадре; точечные — оставшаяся часть каждого пути; штриховая — граница при $t=0$. Add to GLOSSARY 1.11: dotted = «точечная (линия)», dashed = «штриховая», never «пунктирная».

all.title: math.json export.shown_at_t_2, export.deformation_h_t_choice: «H_t переводит тождественное отображение в F» is wrong
all.detail: «f переводит A в B» means f(A) ⊂ B, and the glossary itself uses «переходит в» in that sense. So the sentence says that H_t maps the identity (as a point) to F. The intended meaning is a homotopy that deforms id into F. Шабат and Russian topology courses say «деформирует … в …».
all.fix: export.shown_at_t_2: « Показан кадр при $t={2}$. Здесь $H_t$ непрерывно деформирует тождественное отображение ($t=0$) в {map} ($t={hom.m}$); это {hom.tex}.» For export.deformation_h_t_choice, use the same second and third sentences after «Деформация $H_t${choice}{choice}».

all.title: Two-panel figure captions (figure.js 1262–1271) are not in math.json
all.detail: The main article caption is missing from math.json: «(a) … in the z-plane. (b) Its image under F.» So is the homework caption «… (left) and its image under … (right).» (DESIGN.md row 118 lists them as 'Templates', but no Russian text exists). Russian needs four things here. Subfigure letters «а», «б» in italic. A lower-case shape phrase after the dash. The locative «плоскости». No gendered «его/её», because the shape noun's gender is unknown.
all.fix: Article, two panels: `\textit{а}~--- {list} в~плоскости~${z}$; \textit{б}~--- образ при отображении {map}.{pat}` (plural: «образы»). With no shapes: `\textit{а}~--- плоскость~${z}$; \textit{б}~--- её образ при отображении {map}.` Homework: «Слева — {list}, справа — образ при отображении {wmap}.» (plural «образы»). Left panel only: «{Cap1} в плоскости $z$.» Right panel only: «Образ {list_gen} при отображении {map}.» Note: use lower-case {list}, not {cap1}, after «а —».

all.title: math.json LaTeX preamble comments omit the Cyrillic packages
all.detail: A Russian caption inside the snippet does not compile in pdfLaTeX without T2A and babel ('Command \CYR… unavailable in encoding OT1'). The note on export.if_your_l_narrower says this, but the ru text still says only graphicx,amsmath,amssymb. export.n_pdf_made_for_2 (Beamer) has the same problem and no note.
all.fix: export.if_your_l_narrower: «% Если у вас {L} меньше, укажите [width={L}] (надписи уменьшатся). Преамбула (pdfLaTeX): \usepackage[T2A]{fontenc}\usepackage[russian]{babel}\usepackage{graphicx,amsmath,amssymb}; в XeLaTeX/LuaLaTeX вместо fontenc — \usepackage{fontspec}». export.n_pdf_made_for_2: «… Преамбула: \usepackage[T2A]{fontenc}\usepackage[russian]{babel}\usepackage{graphicx}». Emit these lines only when the caption language is Russian.

all.title: «подписи» is used both for the caption and for the labels inside the figure
all.detail: Russian publishing practice (Мильчин, Чельцова, «Справочник издателя и автора») separates the two. The caption is the «(подрисуночная) подпись». The text in the figure is «надписи». Here, «Подпись» is the caption (export.caption), while export.labels_x_x_pt, export.snippet_includes_figure_at, export.n_pdf_made_for_3 and export.if_your_l_narrower say «подписи» for the tick and axis labels. A reader cannot tell which one shrinks.
all.fix: export.labels_x_x_pt: « · надписи {x}/{x} пт, как в тексте {tsz} пт · {choice} · {choice}». export.snippet_includes_figure_at: «Фрагмент вставляет рисунок в натуральную величину, поэтому надписи на нём совпадают по размеру с вашим текстом.» export.n_pdf_made_for_3: «…, чтобы надписи совпадали по размеру с текстом.» export.if_your_l_narrower: «(надписи уменьшатся)». Add «подпись = caption; надпись = label» to GLOSSARY 1.15.

all.title: math.json export.figure_2 and GLOSSARY 1.11: «В рисунке» should be «На рисунке»
all.detail: In Russian the preposition is «на рисунке» («подпись на рисунке», «на рис. 1»). The JSON itself already says «без подписи на изображении» in export.latex_figure_copied_export.
all.fix: export.figure_2: «На рисунке». In GLOSSARY 1.11, change «в рисунке / только в LaTeX» to «на рисунке / только в LaTeX».

all.title: guide-tour.json tour.each_z_coloured_by: brightness bands are not level sets
all.detail: A level set of |F| is a curve {|F| = c} (Шабат, «линия уровня»). The bands are the regions between such curves. The Russian «полосы яркости — это множества уровня |F|» states something false, and the Russian can be exact even though the English is loose.
all.fix: Каждая точка $z$ окрашена по $\arg F(z)$ (здесь $F(z)=(z^2-1)/(z^2+1)$), а полосы яркости ограничены линиями уровня $|F|$. Все цвета сходятся в нулях $\pm1$ и полюсах $\pm i$: вокруг нуля они идут в одну сторону, вокруг полюса — в другую.

all.title: Notation: arcoth is still not converted (export.homotopy_h_t_v_9, _10, export.c_1_c_v)
all.detail: I ran proto/i18n.js. «\coth(…\operatorname{arcoth}z)» becomes «\operatorname{cth}(…\operatorname{arcoth}z)», which mixes the two notations in one formula. The notes say arcoth → arcth must be added, but RU_OP and RU_PLAIN still lack it. GLOSSARY 2.1 lists arcoth → arcth.
all.fix: Add arcoth: 'arcth' and arccoth: 'arcth' to RU_OP (and to the regex alternation), and arcoth: 'arcth' to RU_PLAIN. Expected: `\operatorname{cth}\bigl((1-t/2)\operatorname{arcth}z\bigr)`.

all.title: Interval punctuation: texDecimal and math.grid_math_min_math contradict GLOSSARY 2.3
all.detail: GLOSSARY 2.3 says: «(0; 1] only when an endpoint has a decimal comma; otherwise (0, 1] as in Russian books» (Шабат, Привалов). texDecimal turns every digit-comma-digit into «;». So $[-1,1]$ becomes $[-1;\,1]$ and $(-\pi/2,3\pi/2)$ becomes $(-\pi/2;\,3\pi/2)$ (export.c_1_c_v), while $(-\pi,\pi]$ keeps its comma. One caption then mixes both styles. math.grid_math_min_math hard-codes «;» as well.
all.fix: Use «;» only when an endpoint contains {,}; otherwise keep «,». Either fix texDecimal, or change the glossary to «always ; in Russian» and apply that everywhere. math.grid_math_min_math: `\text{сетка } [{Math.min}{sep}{Math.max}]\times[{Math.min}{sep}{Math.max}]`, where {sep} is «;\,» if any endpoint is fractional, else «,».

all.title: chrome.json chrome.agrees_on_d_with: the quantifier is ambiguous
all.detail: «для многочленов P и Q» can be read as «for all polynomials». The English means «for some». math.json export.agrees_on_d_with already has the correct «где P и Q — многочлены», so the two files disagree. GLOSSARY 1.10 copies the chrome wording.
all.fix: chrome.agrees_on_d_with: «Совпадает на D с P(z)/Q(z), где P и Q — многочлены.» Update GLOSSARY 1.10 to match.

all.title: chrome.exp_opens_strip_im, chrome.first_quadrant_opens_onto: «в» used where onto («на») is meant
all.detail: GLOSSARY 1.1 says «на» = onto and «в» = into, and asks to keep the difference exactly (Шабат: «отображает D на G»). exp maps the strip onto the right half-plane, and z² maps the quadrant onto the half-plane. In «переводит её в круг», the word «её» is also ambiguous between the strip and the half-plane.
all.fix: chrome.exp_opens_strip_im: «exp отображает полосу |Im z| < π/2 на правую полуплоскость, а дробно-линейное отображение — эту полуплоскость на круг.» chrome.first_quadrant_opens_onto: «Первая четверть отображается на верхнюю полуплоскость; углы в точке 0 удваиваются.»

all.title: «то есть» should be «поэтому» in the conformal tooltip (chrome.analytic_injective_biholomorphism_d, GLOSSARY 1.10)
all.detail: F′ ≠ 0 for a univalent holomorphic function is a theorem (Шабат), not a restatement. math.json export.holomorphic_injective_hence_biholomorphism correctly says «поэтому … причём F′ ≠ 0». The two files disagree.
all.fix: chrome.analytic_injective_biholomorphism_d: «Функция F голоморфна и однолистна, поэтому задаёт биголоморфное отображение D → F(D), причём F′ ≠ 0.» Make the same change in GLOSSARY 1.10.

all.title: math.json export.w_k_w_k: «bypassed» is translated as «пропущен», not «отключён»
all.detail: The glossary (1.8) and chrome.bypassed use «отключён» for a step bypassed by the jumper. «пропущен» is reserved for a step skipped because of an error (export.w_k_w_k_2). With «пропущен» in both, the LaTeX cannot tell the two cases apart.
all.fix: w_{{k}} &= w_{{k}} && \text{(шаг {k} отключён)}

all.title: chrome.json chrome.right_click_circle_around: «разрыв» suggests a discontinuity
all.detail: The running integral is continuous. It simply does not return to its starting value. «разрыв» is the term for a discontinuity.
all.fix: Щёлкните окружность правой кнопкой: при обходе полюса i интеграл с переменным верхним пределом не возвращается к начальному значению — разность равна 2πi · Res = π.

all.title: chrome.json chrome.conformal_on_injective_on: «полосах высоты 2π»
all.detail: The standard wording is «однолистна в (любой горизонтальной) полосе ширины 2π» (Шабат, ЛШ). «высота» of a strip is not used, and for analytic maps the glossary prefers «однолистно».
all.fix: Конформно на ℂ; однолистно в любой горизонтальной полосе ширины 2π

all.title: export.color_shows_f_key: tautology «линии — линии уровня», and a mismatch with export.bar_lines_are_level
all.detail: «линии — линии уровня» repeats the word. The fragment export.bar_lines_are_level already says «показаны линии уровня». GLOSSARY §4 example 18 has the same tautology.
all.fix: export.color_shows_f_key: «: цвет показывает $\arg {f}$ (шкала справа); проведены линии уровня $|{f}|$ и $\arg {f}$.» Change GLOSSARY §4 #18 the same way («…(шкала справа); проведены линии уровня…»).

all.title: Different verbs for the same phenomena across the three files
all.detail: Zeros and poles that fly in from infinity: «приходят из бесконечности» (math.critical_points_fly_from, math.poles_critical_points_fly, export.zoom_homotopy_h_t_3) versus «прилетают» (guide.deformation_top_bar_x). The jump at the cut: «скачет» (chrome.landscape_with_all_sheets) versus «прыгает» (tour.landscape_all_sheets_draws). Both «скачет» and «прыгает» are colloquial for a jump discontinuity.
all.fix: guide.deformation_top_bar_x: «…поэтому их нули, полюсы и разрезы приходят из бесконечности (sin(tz)/t)…». chrome.landscape_with_all_sheets: «Рельеф, все листы: Im Ln z поднимается по геликоиду вокруг 0, а не терпит скачка на разрезе.» tour.landscape_all_sheets_draws: «… $\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Ln} z$ поднимается по геликоиду вокруг $0$, а не терпит скачка на разрезе.»

all.title: The order of a zero is in the genitive in one file and the nominative in another
all.detail: export.order_r_mult gives « (порядка {r.mult})», while sound.order_p_mult gives « (порядок {p.mult})». In a list after a colon («Нули (точки): $0$ (…)»), the nominative reads naturally.
all.fix: export.order_r_mult: « (порядок {r.mult})»

all.title: Caption fragments end with a one-letter preposition followed by an ordinary space
all.detail: GLOSSARY 3.6 requires a no-break space after one-letter words in captions. These fragments are glued directly to a formula: export.brightness_increases_with («вместе с »), export.by_factors («растёт в »), export.here_chain_built_step («начиная с »).
all.fix: Replace the trailing space with U+00A0 (`~` in LaTeX): «яркость растёт вместе с », « растёт в », « Здесь цепочка строится по шагам, начиная с ».

all.title: «Справка» and «Руководство» are mixed for the guide
all.detail: GLOSSARY 1.13 has Help (menu) = «Справка» and Guide (reference) = «Руководство». The tour says «{?} сразу открывает руководство» and the keys list says «Это руководство», but chrome.open_guide says «Открыть справку».
all.fix: chrome.open_guide: «Открыть руководство». Keep chrome.guide «Справка  ?» only if the button also opens the tour; otherwise use «Руководство  ?».

all.title: «выбранной» and «выделенной» are both used for a selected shape
all.detail: GLOSSARY 1.8 says a selected shape is «выделенная фигура». chrome.integrate_along_selected_curve uses «выбранной», and chrome.select_closed_curve_or and chrome.cauchy_style_select_closed say «Выберите», while the tour says «выделите».
all.fix: chrome.integrate_along_selected_curve: «Вычислить интеграл по выделенной кривой». chrome.select_closed_curve_or: «Выделите замкнутую кривую или ограниченную область — будет показан её интеграл Коши.» chrome.cauchy_style_select_closed: «Стиль «Интеграл Коши»: выделите замкнутую кривую или ограниченную область, чтобы увидеть её интеграл Коши.»

all.title: Small wording points
all.detail: tour.pattern_painted_on_x: the pattern name is not in quotes, unlike «Клетки» and «Растяжение». chrome.circle_through_1_becomes: «крыло»; the glossary term is «профиль (крыла)». math.m_bius ru_short «Мёбиус» contradicts GLOSSARY 1.2. math.what_not_holomorphic_has: «не голоморфная функция». math.formula_undefined_for_every: «логарифма от 0». export.typesetter_still_loading_try: «Набор формул» names the process, not the program. export.figure_at_printed_size: «в размере печати». guide.sound_top_bar_x: a pitch class cannot «равен arg F».
all.fix: tour.pattern_painted_on_x: «…; «Лог-полярные клетки» при конформном отображении остаются квадратными; …». chrome.circle_through_1_becomes: «Окружность, проходящая через 1, переходит в профиль крыла с острой задней кромкой.» math.m_bius: drop ru_short (or use «Дробно-линейная»). math.what_not_holomorphic_has: «{what} не является голоморфной функцией (у неё нет комплексной производной), поэтому эту формулу нельзя дифференцировать по z». math.formula_undefined_for_every: «…или логарифма нуля)». export.typesetter_still_loading_try: «Модуль вёрстки формул ещё загружается; попробуйте чуть позже.» export.figure_at_printed_size: «Рисунок в печатном размере». guide.sound_top_bar_x: «…тон, звуковысотный класс которого задаётся значением arg F…».

all.title: GLOSSARY.md: entries to add or correct so it matches the fixes above
all.detail: Several glossary entries need updating. 1.15 lacks «сравнение» (congruence), «подпись/надпись» and «пунктир». 1.10 has «то есть» and «для многочленов P и Q». 1.11 has «в рисунке», and its example caption uses a gendered «его образ» that the templates cannot know. §4 #18 has the tautology. 2.5 says babel-russian defines \tg… «only at \begin{document} and only when Russian is loaded», but DESIGN.md line 134 says «in every language, robust»; one of the two is wrong. The conclusion (\operatorname) holds either way.
all.fix: Add rows to 1.15: «сравнение | congruence mod m | inequality → неравенство; the symbol → знак сравнения»; «подпись | caption | labels in the figure → надписи»; «пунктирная | (avoid) | dotted → точечная; dashed → штриховая». In 1.10: «поэтому … причём F′ ≠ 0» and «где P и Q — многочлены». In 1.11: «на рисунке» and «а — круг |z| < 1; б — образ при отображении F». Fix §4 #18. Re-test 2.5 and make DESIGN.md agree.

all.title: Spelling error: «неограниченна»
all.detail: chrome.unbounded_drawn_about_200 has «Фигура неограниченна: …». In mathematical Russian the short form is «не ограничена», written as two words with one «н», as in «функция не ограничена». The double «нн» form is a spelling error.
all.fix: chrome.unbounded_drawn_about_200: «Фигура не ограничена: она рисуется примерно на 200 ширин вида и бледнеет к краю.»

all.title: Zero and pole lists drop «or more» and «and more»
all.detail: The English template is '{n}{ or more} zero{s}: {items}{, and more}'. The Russian is «{n} нулей: {items}» (plurals included), so both 'or more' and 'and more' are lost. The screen reader then reports an exact count when the search was cut short. The note on the entry already says «не менее» needs genitive forms, but no forms are given. sound.extra.list_poles has the same problem.
all.fix: Give both entries a split exact/atLeast, like chrome.extra.n_preimages_of, and add the tail {andMore} (= sound.more, fixed below). sound.extra.list_zeros: exact one «{n} нуль: {items}{andMore}», few «{n} нуля: …», many «{n} нулей: …», other «{n} нуля: …». atLeast one «не менее {n} нуля: {items}{andMore}», few/many «не менее {n} нулей: …», other «не менее {n} нуля: …». sound.extra.list_poles: exact one «{n} полюс: …», few «{n} полюса: …», many «{n} полюсов: …», other «{n} полюса: …». atLeast one «не менее {n} полюса: …», few/many «не менее {n} полюсов: …», other «не менее {n} полюса: …».

all.title: «проигрывать» also means 'to lose'
all.detail: Some phrases read as a loss. «замкнутая петля проигрывает своё число оборотов» can be read as 'the loop loses its winding number'. «Проигрывает гомотопию» and «кривую здесь не проиграть» have the same problem. The glossary itself uses «воспроизвести» for play. Affected ids: tour.plays_homotopy_h_t, guide.deformation_top_bar_x, tour.sound_stays_off_until, tour.sound_stays_off_until_2, tour.sound_stays_off_until_3, sound.curve_cannot_be_played, sound.more_turns_than_can, and GLOSSARY.md section 4, example 20.
all.fix: tour.plays_homotopy_h_t: «Эта кнопка воспроизводит гомотопию $H_t$ от тождественного отображения до $F$ — шаг за шагом, во всех видах. all.title: Overall verdict (what passed)
all.detail: These checks passed across all three tables. Form of address: «вы» in lower case, plural imperative, no «мы», no «давайте», no exclamation marks. Commands use the infinitive; openers use nouns. Spelling: ё is written everywhere it belongs. Quotes are «ёлочки» with no straight quotes in visible text. The em dash has a no-break space before it in every string (lint: 0 misses). Words match the glossary: «нуль», «полюсы», «круг» vs «окружность», «прямая», «образ», «при отображении», «LaTeX-код». The plural tables (one/few/many/other) are grammatical for every governing word I checked («не более 21 нуля», «2 корня», «не менее 5 прообразов»). Tour copy mostly reads like a calm teacher; the items above are the exceptions. Not checked: on-screen overflow at 360 px. I also did not re-review the provisional figure.js strings against the live dialog.
all.fix: None needed beyond the items above.

all.title: Inventory misses many visible strings, mostly figure captions
all.detail:
I spot-checked the base src against inventory.json. 40 of the 129 caption segments `{t:'...'}` in app.js are missing. They are at lines 4794, 4815, 4827, 4856, 4859, 4874, 8976-8996 (shape descriptions such as 'the segment ' and 'a polygon with N vertices'), 9018-9025 (pattern sentences), 9047, 9054, 9119 ('Where the formula is defined,', 'On its natural domain') and 9324. Also missing:
- the DC_STYLES phase-style tooltips and the labels 'Modulus' and 'Contours' (app.js:6555)
- the tooltip suffixes 'Turn off Deformation (M) to draw' and 'Draw in Plane' (app.js:3014)
- 'Drag to draw a/an {lab}', which picks the English article with /^[aeiou]/ (app.js:6567)
- 'Image after adding f_k' (app.js:8577)
- tour toasts and status lines (tour.js:759, 1148, 1150, 1201, 1215)
- the funcs.js homotopy captions at lines 101 (loxodromic) and 323 (power homotopy)
The translators' ru/chrome.json already needed '.extra.' keys for strings the inventory lacks.
all.fix: Re-run the extractor so it takes every literal inside caption-segment arrays and template literals. Widen its list of sinks: dataset.tip, toast, call('toast'), say, sndSay and canvas fillText. Make the gate a browser check: 'no English left' in Russian over every view, menu, dialog, toast and tooltip. Do not rely on the hand-read inventory.

all.title: Language button changes the English header, and the identity test hides it
all.detail: The decided default puts the Language setting in the More menu and the command palette. The prototype instead adds #langBtn, a globe icon, to the English header at every width (page.html, and visible in the 1440 px shots). The rule is that English stays exactly as it is. proto/browser/behave.js skips this button (`if (el.closest('#langBtn')) continue;`), so the 'English DOM identical' result only holds because of that exclusion.
all.fix: Show the button only inside the collapsed header menu (hdrMenu) at phone widths, plus the palette commands. Hide it at docked widths with a CSS rule, and keep that rule as one switch in case the user wants the button. Then remove the #langBtn exclusion from the identity check.

all.title: Switching language during the tour or with blocked storage loses work
all.detail:
onSwitch calls writeState(), stashes {hist, hi} in sessionStorage and reloads.
- During the tour (xt), tourHold makes writeState a no-op, but hist holds the tour's scenes. After the reload, Undo steps into tour scenes on top of the user's work.
- When storage is blocked (private window, claude.ai), the preference cannot be written either. The reload then throws away all unsaved work, and the language does not change.
all.fix: In setPref, first check that the preference and the state can be written and read back. If they cannot, do not reload; show a toast instead. If a tour holds the canvas, end it and restore the user's work before saving, or never stash hist while tourHold is set. Add both cases to behave.js.

all.title: {name} placeholders collide with TeX groups; 35 inventory placeholders cannot be filled
all.detail: fill() replaces `{x}` whenever params has x. Templates that carry math, such as `$H_t({v})={v}^{{n}}$` (funcs.js), contain literal TeX groups like `^{n}`, `_{k}` and `e^{t}`. When a parameter has the same name, the literal group is silently replaced. The node test compares tokens, so it cannot catch this. Separately, 35 inventory texts use placeholders that the fill regex `[A-Za-z_]\w*` never matches: {2}, {1}, {j}, {alpha.re} (for example app.js:834 'all steps · t = {2}').
all.fix: Use a placeholder syntax that TeX never produces, for example `{{name}}` or `%{name}`, at least for templates that contain math. Rename the inventory placeholders to identifiers. Add an extractor test: the placeholders of each call site's literal must equal the keys of the params it passes.

all.title: The plural scheme and its test block correct Russian plurals
all.detail:
$tn keys the entry on the English `one` string, and t_i18n.js requires every Russian form to have the same placeholders as that `one` string.
- English one-forms often have no {n} ('A zero and a pole cancel'). Russian 'one' also covers 21, 31 and 101, so its forms need {n}. The test forbids exactly the correct translation.
- Two pairs with the same singular collide.
- The inventory flags 49 plural strings, including fragment plurals such as item/items/was/were (app.js:11873).
all.fix: Key plural entries on `one + \u0004 + many`, or on the `many` form. Require {n} in the Russian few/many/other forms and check them against `many`. Keep sentences meant for exactly 1 as an `n === 1` branch in code, and use $tn only for the counted sentence.

all.title: Letter shortcuts from the sound and export work are not on the Russian-layout list
all.detail:
The §7 table and the key test cover only the base handler.
- xr/xs add ⌘E (figure export) and ⇧M (sound). They read `key`, so they work only if the merge keeps keyOf.
- sndKey (xr app.js:12020) matches Z, O, D and L with `e.key.toLowerCase()`. On ЙЦУКЕН these keys give я, щ, в and д, so the sound keyboard fails.
all.fix: Send sndKey through I18N.keyOf. Add ⌘E, ⇧M and sound Z, O, D, L to the §7 table. Extend behave.js so that every letter shortcut is fired with its Cyrillic e.key plus e.code: V P S L R C A F D B G O H N K T M Z, ⌘Z ⇧⌘Z ⌘Y ⌘K ⌘E ⇧M, the sound keys and [ ].

all.title: texDecimal on whole snippets would break the LaTeX
all.detail:
DESIGN §5 applies I18N.texDecimal() to Russian captions and snippets.
- The figure snippet (xr figure.js:1347 and 1355) contains `\ifdim\linewidth<${w}pt` with a decimal w such as 469.75. texDecimal turns it into `469{,}75pt`, which is a TeX error.
- The second regex rewrites any `}, <digit>` into `;\,`, so a formula followed by a condition is changed too.
all.fix: Never run a regex over finished TeX. Write the decimal comma where numbers are formatted (CX.texNum and fmtNum taking a lang argument), only inside caption math. Leave the snippet body, the preamble and all dimensions alone. Add a test that compiles the generated Russian snippet, not a hand-written one.

all.title: Notation gaps: arcoth, Res, the multivalued log and parser holes
all.detail:
- `\operatorname{arcoth}` appears 3 times in funcs.js and is not in RU_OP. The Russian caption then mixes 'cth(... arcoth w)'. GLOSSARY says arcth.
- `\operatorname{Res}` has no decision. Шабат and Лаврентьев–Шабат write res; Свешников–Тихонов write выч.
- The blanket `\log`→`\ln` rule mislabels the multivalued logarithm. Example: tour.js:176, 'All sheets ... Im log z climbs a helicoid' must read Ln in Russian. DESIGN says the app never shows the multivalued log, but it does.
- Parser (probed): `arcctg` is not accepted in either form. There is no acot at all, so RU_OP's arccot→arcctg can never fire. `Ln z` and `lg z` fail with 'Unknown symbol L' and 'Unknown symbol l'.
all.fix: Add arcoth→arcth. Decide res, and prefer upright `\operatorname{res}` (Cyrillic выч inside math would need the CMU path). Mark multivalued uses in the English source, for example with a 'multi' context or a dedicated macro, and map them to `\operatorname{Ln}` in Russian; let the test allow that. In the parser, accept Ln the way Log is accepted (principal branch, documented). Either add acot with arccot and arcctg, or give a specific Russian error. Give lg a clear message.

all.title: I18N.using() does not survive the async figure build
all.detail: An English caption from the Russian UI uses I18N.using('en', fn), which only covers synchronous code. The figure build awaits MathJax and the lazily fetched CMU tables. notation(), texDecimal() and num() default to the UI language, and XD.tex applies notation() at render time. Strings and TeX built after an await therefore come out in Russian: tg, ln, decimal commas, «Рис.» or а/б panel letters in an 'English' figure.
all.fix: Store the caption language in the figure object (fig.lang). Pass it explicitly to t/tx/tn (as an option), notation(tex, lang), texDecimal, cyrWord, panel letters and 'Figure n.'. Test: Russian UI with an English caption gives an SVG, a PDF and a snippet with no Cyrillic and no tg.

all.title: More code reads its own English text than DESIGN lists
all.detail:
DESIGN names two cases (figure.js:1199 and the /Save/ test). There are more:
- app.js:7251 `textContent === sub.label` (submenu back-navigation).
- xr app.js:2285 and 9010 decide whether a label is a word with `/[A-Za-z]{2}|\s/`. A one-word Cyrillic label such as 'Круг' is set as math, so it renders as MathJax italic and exports as a `<text>` fallback. This also affects Russian users of the English UI.
- xr app.js:8330 compares the palette query with the English d.label.
- tour.js helpWhere() returns 'Help' and '⋯ › Help', which must match the translated button names.
all.fix: Use ids or flags instead of comparing label text. Use `/\p{L}{2}|\s/u`. Build helpWhere from the same keys as the buttons. Add a grep test that forbids comparisons and regexes on UI text.

all.title: CMU glyph table has no Latin letters; Russian caption typography rules are missing
all.detail: cyrWord handles any `\text{}` word that contains Cyrillic, but the table holds only Cyrillic, punctuation and digits. A mixed word, such as the user label 'Круг-A' or 'PDF-файл', falls back to MathJax `<text>` and fails the outline-only preflight. Caption line breaking also lacks Russian rules: a no-break space after one-letter words (в, к, с, о, у, и, а), before the em dash, and in 'Рис. 1'.
all.fix: Split words into runs by script (Latin to MathJax, Cyrillic to CMU), or add Basic Latin to the tables (about +6 KB gzip). In the Russian caption layout, insert no-break spaces after one-letter prepositions and conjunctions, before ' — ', and between 'Рис.' and its number.

all.title: Font loading race and unmeasured canvas text
all.detail: applyPage() adds the stylesheet and calls document.fonts.load() straight away. The @font-face rules do not exist yet, so the call loads nothing. The app redraws only on the first document.fonts.ready. Canvas text, which uses TH.ui from --f-ui, can stay in the fallback face until the next interaction. That covers the legend ('Scale |F′|', 'Pattern', 'left view') and plot labels ('pole ×2'), 26 fillText sites in all. The legend canvas has a fixed size (272×144, so about 136 CSS px), and pseudo-localization never reaches canvas text, so Russian legend widths were never measured.
all.fix: On link.onload, await fonts.load for the faces, then clear rulerCache and request a render (or listen for document.fonts 'loadingdone'). Measure the Russian legend strings, and widen the legend canvas under :root[data-lang="ru"] if they need it.

all.title: Archivo Latin next to Roboto Flex Cyrillic on the same line
all.detail: Per-character fallback keeps Latin, digits and punctuation in Archivo and sets Cyrillic in Roboto Flex. Every Russian label that mixes scripts ('Сохранить PDF', 'Формула 1', 'LaTeX-код') shows two typeface designs side by side, which is not article-grade. Greek letters that Archivo lacks also move from the system font to Roboto Flex Greek, which is an extra fetch. Google CSS confirms the cyrillic subsets for Roboto Flex and JetBrains Mono, so coverage itself is fine.
all.fix: Under :root[data-lang="ru"], put Roboto Flex first in --f-ui so a Russian line uses one face. English is unaffected. Keep B612 Mono first for values. Decide with a specimen of mixed-script labels at 11-13 px in light and dark themes.

all.title: Decimal comma on screen clashes with formula input
all.detail: Readouts show '0,5', but the parser rejects 'z^0,5' and '0,5*z' with "Unexpected ','" (probed). Russian users will type what they see. num() replaces only the point, so a readout of two numbers becomes '(0,5, 0,3)', which is ambiguous.
all.fix: Keep the point on screen and use the comma only in exported captions and LaTeX (flip DECIMAL_COMMA for the screen), or ask the user. If the comma stays on screen, add a parser hint for digit,digit ('Десятичная точка: 0.5') and use '; ' between numbers in readouts.

all.title: Pseudo-localization underestimates expansion
all.detail: A uniform +35 % on text that stays mostly Latin under-measures short labels, which Russian lengthens by 50-100 % (Fit view → Вписать в окно, Hide → Скрыть, Compact → Компактно). The run never reached canvas text, the CSS content 'Preview', or the xr figure dialog. The real-Russian overflow run used page.html strings only. The 14 hotspots are therefore a lower bound.
all.fix: Scale the pseudo expansion by length: about +100 % up to 5 characters, +60 % up to 20, +35 % beyond. Hook canvas text through a fillText wrapper in pseudo mode. Make the gate the full Russian table run with 'no new overflow' across the width × theme matrix.

all.title: Translation files and the gettext key scheme do not match
all.detail: ru/chrome.json, ru/math.json and ru/guide-tour.json are keyed by inventory id with {en, ru, ru_short}. i18n.js keys by the English source. The same English text with different Russian in different places ('Close', 'Plain', 'Tiles', 'Region') collides silently. ru_short has no mechanism. §11 step 6 does not describe the conversion.
all.fix: Write a converter that groups entries by English text. When the Russian differs, it assigns $tx contexts (card, heading, pred, lamp, short) and reports the call sites that need a context. Map ru_short to the 'short' context. The node test should fail on unresolved collisions.

all.title: Inventory marks identifiers as translatable
all.detail: Entries that are not UI text: 'export' (app.js:1306, a `why` reason code), 'circle' (region.js:1552, a CAP_FAMILY value) and 'amsart' (figure.js:463, a LaTeX class name). The param labels sheet, branch, zeros and poles appear both as entries and on the do-not-translate list, but the entries carry no hazard. In total 147 entries overlap the do-not-translate list without a flag on the entry.
all.fix: Drop the three identifiers. Mark the param labels as 'display through a map; the key stays English'. Record do-not-translate reasons as hazards on the entries themselves.

all.title: The table ships inside the English page in the prototype
all.detail: work/xl/build.py inlines ru.json in every build, English included. The full table is about 250 KB, roughly 70 KB gzip, which is 12 % of today's page. The '--inline-i18n' single-file option keeps that cost for English users.
all.fix: Do §11 step 7 (a separate i18n/ru.json fetched only in Russian) before any English perf or quality gate. Test that the artifact's supporting-file fetch works on claude.ai and on GitHub Pages. Never inline the table in builds published for English.

all.title: i18n.js robustness: parts() on plural entries, prototype keys, unbounded `missing`
all.detail:
- parts() calls s.slice and s.length on the entry object when the entry is a plural, which crashes or drops the tail.
- Tables are plain objects, so a key such as 'constructor' returns a function and tn() crashes.
- In Russian, every lookup miss goes into the `missing` Set. With the h() crutch and dynamic readouts it grows for the whole session.
all.fix: In parts(), normalise the entry to a string first. Build tables with Object.create(null) or check hasOwnProperty. Record misses only under ?lang= or a debug flag, with a size cap.

all.title: English is not quite untouched; the '/' key on Russian PC layouts
all.detail:
- applyPage() sets <html lang="en"> in English too. That is harmless, but it contradicts 'English does nothing'.
- On ЙЦУКЕН-PC, the key printed with '/' types '.', so the palette key needs Shift+\.
- The language menu shows the current choice as '✓' in the key slot, with no menuitemradio or aria-checked.
all.fix: Touch lang only when the language is not English. Also accept e.code 'Slash' without Shift as the palette key, after checking that no layout maps a shortcut there. Use role=menuitemradio with aria-checked for the language items.

all.title: LaTeX and PDF details for Russian exports
all.detail:
- The beamer frame title ('Phase portrait of $F$') and the snippet comments are English. The slides preamble comment lacks T2A and babel for Cyrillic.
- The PDF info Subject is raw caption TeX. jsPDF may write Cyrillic there in PDFDocEncoding, which shows as mojibake.
- An English-main document that takes a Russian caption gets no Russian hyphenation.
all.fix: Translate the frame title and comments, and give the Russian preamble comment for slides too. Write the info strings as UTF-16BE with a BOM, and check them in the PDF (pdfinfo). Mention `\foreignlanguage{russian}{...}` in the snippet comment.

all.title: Points not yet settled in the plan: caption switch, texSpeech, node globals
all.detail:
- If the caption-language switch shows in the English export dialog, it changes English.
- texSpeech (app.js about line 7549) builds spoken formula text from English words. DESIGN does not cover it.
- Once parse.js and funcs.js call $t, every node test needs global $t, but i18n.js exports only I18N.
all.fix: Show the caption switch only when the UI is not English (one switch), or ask the user. Give texSpeech its own Russian grammar using fnName, not word-by-word $t. Have i18n.js set globalThis.$t, $tx and $tn, or add a shared test preload.

all.title: Operator names render bold in the Russian caption demo
all.detail: In shots-ru/cyr_caption.png the operator names Im (in 0 < Im z < π) and tg (in w = tg z) are drawn heavier than the surrounding math, as if taken from the bold glyph set used for «Рис. 1.». Operator names must be upright regular, as pdfLaTeX sets \operatorname{tg} and \operatorname{Im}.
all.fix: Find where the caption composer picks the glyph set for \operatorname / \mathrm runs after a bold label and reset it; re-render the demo and compare with latex/pdflatex_p-1.png.

all.title: The demo caption writes [−1; 1] although neither endpoint is a decimal
all.detail: README rule 5 says a semicolon inside brackets only when an endpoint is a decimal, so [−1, 1]. The demo caption in shots-ru/cyr_caption.png shows «отрезок [−1; 1]».
all.fix: Make the demo follow texDecimal()/the rule (or fix the rule if the demo is right) and re-render.
